messages:
nate: Heads up — ran a focused perf pass on Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B with the new batch-affinity steering and an updated kernel-selection heuristic. dropping concise notes here.

eva: TL;DR numbers?

nate: TL;DR: Mistral-7B (RoPE scale=1.15, headscale=1.7) using kernel-A via the new chooser: ~12% p95 improvement vs baseline. AWQ-int8 calibration gives ~0.7% accuracy drop on studio-100. Qwen-7B: smaller latency win but larger accuracy regression under AWQ (~1.6%). details below.

hao: paste microbench logs + exact configs? which batching window did you run?

nate: batching window: dynamic 8ms, microbatch cap 32, affinity steering enabled (prefer same-GPU microbatches when KV hotset present). reproducer: `eng-run perf --model mistral-7b --profile batch-affinity --warmup 200 --iters 1500`.

nate: microbench snippets: 
``nMistral-7B (fp16, kernel=A)
throughput: 650 tok/s
p50: 9.8ms
p95: 33.2ms
median GPU mem: 5.7GB

Mistral-7B (awq-int8, kernel=A)
throughput: 720 tok/s
p50: 8.6ms
p95: 29.5ms
studio-100 acc delta: -0.7%

Qwen-7B (fp16, kernel=B)
p95: 41.1ms

Qwen-7B (awq-int8, kernel=B)
p95: 37.0ms
studio-100 acc delta: -1.6%
```

jin: Qwen's accuracy hit is non-trivial. do we know if AWQ or kernel choice is the primary cause?

eva: did a quick bisect: AWQ quantization accounts for most of the Qwen delta. picking kernel-B vs kernel-C changes the observed delta (kernel choice can mitigate ~0.4% in the experiments). kernel selection matters.

hao: KV cache behavior? did affinity steering help reduce evictions or KV migration?

nate: yes — enabling affinity reduced tail latency by ~10% on synthetic hotset workload (hotset=top 10% of contexts) by reducing KV slot migration. we observed KV spill-to-host for long sequences (>=4096) when prefetch_horizon < 3.

nate: KV-spill reproducer:
```
python tools/repro.py --model mistral-7b --seq 4600 --prefetch 2 --run-id kv-spill-2439
# logs in /tmp/repro/kv-spill-2439
```

eva: maybe prefetch_horizon auto-tune should scale with RoPE/headscale. RoPE scaling changes activation magnitude and memory locality.

jin: sketched autotune: prefetch_horizon = clamp(2, 16, int(base_horizon * (rope_scale / 1.0) * (headscale / 1.0)))) — will test tomorrow.

hao: what calibration set for AWQ/GPTQ? and exact quant command?

nate: calib set: `calib-small` (2k short diverse prompts covering math, code, QA). command: `quantize-tool awq --model mistral-7b --calib-set data/calib-small.jsonl --out models/mistral-7b-awq-int8 --per-channel`.

eva: any per-layer sensitivity? which layers show the largest drift after AWQ?

nate: Mistral: mid-to-late layers (18-26) show larger drift; Qwen: projection/MLP around layers 12-16 sensitive. mid-layer KL divergence spikes to ~0.035 vs baseline ~0.009 in the noisy cases.

jin: idea: kernel-chooser could prefer kernel-C for layers with high per-layer KL under quantization. avoids some generation regressions.

hao: did canary runs show production regressions?

nate: tiny canary (2% traffic) for mistral-awq-int8+affinity: p95 improved but code-generation error rate rose 0.4% -> 1.1% (mirrors studio delta).

nate: proposed mitigation:
- revert AWQ-int8 default for Qwen until per-layer compensations exist
- set kernel-A as preferred for Mistral in Dedicated, with canary gate: allow <= -0.3% studio-100 drop
- enable auto-prefetch tuning that scales with rope/headscale and seq-length distribution
- add kernel hysteresis (don't flip kernel on <5000 requests) to avoid thrash

eva: agree on hysteresis. add rollout doc + CI perf job to run studio-100 weekly and flag deltas > 0.5%.

jin: i'll add per-layer KL probe + a fallback rule in kernel-chooser: if layer_kl > 0.02 and quant==awq then prefer kernel-C for that layer.

hao: checklist:
- jin: implement per-layer probe + chooser rule
- nate: add auto-prefetch heuristic + KV-spill reproducer artifacts
- eva: update canary thresholds and CI eval job
- ops-bot: schedule a 1-hour canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC

ops-bot: scheduled canary: mistral-awq-int8-affinity on prod-dedicated-1 at 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z (owner: ops)

nate: i'll upload reproducer logs and open the KL-probe PR shortly.

eva: main point: AWQ-int8 is cost-attractive; we need model- and layer-aware safety nets rather than blanket blocks.

jin: quick follow-up: experimental fp8 paths show similar perf with <0.2% acc delta but limited hardware availability — worth tracking.

eva: thanks all, keep PR comments short and tag @eng-runtime for reviews :thumbsup:

nate: closing thread once PRs land.
